openingMessage: The difference between a successful person and others is not a lack of strength, not a lack of knowledge, but rather a lack of will.
openingWhy: Every hand on this crew can recite the five-point check in his sleep. Knowledge was never the gap. The gap shows up at hour eleven on job four, when knowing and doing start to separate — and will is the only thing that holds them together.
leadershipThought: Awareness means you notice things before they become incidents — the crossing traffic at the gate, the eyes drooping in the driver's seat, the speed creeping up. That is not luck. That is discipline built over time.

specialFocus.title: Driver's License — On You, Every Drive. It's the Law.
specialFocus.why: Driving week closes on the simplest requirement of all — the one in your wallet. Texas law (Transportation Code 521.025) requires you to have your driver's license IN YOUR POSSESSION any time you operate a vehicle and to show it when a peace officer asks. No license on you at a stop means a citation and a roadside identity check that can hold up you, the truck, and the job — and in a company vehicle it's not just your problem. Every one of us drives for a living before we do anything else for a living: a legal, licensed, carried-on-you driver is step zero of journey management. The gear gets inspected every month — this morning, the wallet does too.
specialFocus.standardLabel: The License Standard — Thirty Seconds, Right Now
standard: License ON YOU every single drive — wallet or clip, not the console of your other truck, not at the house. Texas Transportation Code 521.025: in your possession while operating, shown on demand. Pull it out right now and physically check it this morning.

Check the EXPIRATION date while it's in your hand. An expired license means you are not a legal driver — in a company truck that exposes you, the company, and our insurance. If it's expired or inside 30 days of expiring, tell your lead TODAY and get it renewed.
Address current? Texas gives you 30 days after a move to update it (521.054). Takes five minutes online — do it this weekend if you've moved.

Anything that threatens your license — a suspension, an unpaid ticket, a court date, a DWI charge — your lead hears it from YOU before you drive, not from a DOT stop after. No judgment call at the wheel: not legal, not driving, we work it out.

Carry the full packet: license, current insurance card for the truck, and your medical card if your position requires one. A clean traffic stop takes two minutes; a scramble takes an hour and an incident report.

scenarios.title: The Routine Stop That Wasn't
scenarios.body: A tech gets stopped for a plate light on the way to location at 5 AM. License is in his other jacket. What should have been a two-minute warning becomes forty-five minutes on the shoulder while the officer verifies identity, a citation under 521.025, and a late arrival the company man notices. Nothing unsafe happened — and it still cost the job, the schedule, and a mark on our name with the customer. The fix costs nothing: it's a wallet check before the key turns.

questions: Everyone take out your license right now — who found an expiration date inside the next 60 days?
Where does your license physically ride on a workday — and is that with you on every vehicle swap, truck to truck?
If something put your license at risk tomorrow — a ticket, a court date — who do you call first and when?
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: License on your person, valid and current, every time you turn a key — Texas law and Canon's. If your license is at risk, your lead knows before the truck moves.
